cellpose:
Runs Cellpose on the input image. This node supports both segmentation in 3D and executing Cellpose for each 2D image plane. This node can generate a multitude of outputs, although only ROI is activated by default. Go to the 'Outputs' parameter section to enable the other outputs.
  • Labels: A grayscale image where each connected component is assigned a unique value. Please note that ImageJ will run into issues if too many objects are present and the labels are saved in int32. ImageJ would load them as float32.
  • Flows: An RGB image that indicates the flow of each pixel. Convert it to HSB to extract information.
  • Probabilities: An image indicating the probabilities for each pixel.
  • Styles: A vector summarizing each image.
  • ROI: ROI of the segmented areas.

Trains a segmentation model with Cellpose. You start from an existing model or train from scratch. Incoming images are automatically converted to greyscale. Only 2D or 3D images are supported. For this node to work, you need to annotate a greyscale 16-bit or 8-bit label image column to each raw data input. To do this, you can use the node 'Annotate with data'. By default, JIPipe will ensure that all connected components of this image are assigned a unique component. You can disable this feature via the parameters. Does not support the training of image restoration models.

Deprecated

This node uses Cellpose 3-era training defaults (learning rate 0.2, weight decay 1e-5, 500 epochs) that are not optimized for Cellpose 4's transformer-based architecture. Use the non-deprecated 'Cellpose segmentation training (4.x)' node instead, which has correct defaults for fine-tuning transformer models (learning rate 1e-5, weight decay 0.1, 100 epochs).
cellpose-segmentation-training-4.x-v2:
Trains a segmentation model with Cellpose 4.2+. Cellpose 4 uses transformer-based architectures (SAM-ViTL for cpsam, DINOv3 for cpdino) that are pre-trained on large datasets and converge faster than the U-Net-based Cellpose 2/3.

Recommended workflow

  • Start from cpsam: Only the built-in cpsam model is recommended as a starting point for fine-tuning. Starting from other models can produce suboptimal results.
  • Low learning rate: The default learning rate of 1e-5 is critical. Higher rates can destabilize the pre-trained transformer backbone and lead to poor results.
  • Fewer epochs: Transformer models converge in 100 epochs (default), unlike U-Net-based Cellpose 2/3 which typically need 500. Monitor the training loss — if it stops decreasing, fewer epochs are sufficient.
  • Batch size 1: Transformer models require significant GPU memory. Use a batch size of 1 unless you have a high-memory GPU.
  • Weight decay 0.1: Helps prevent overfitting on small datasets, which is especially important for transformer fine-tuning.

Data preparation

Incoming images are automatically converted to greyscale. Only 2D or 3D images are supported. For this node to work, you need to annotate a greyscale 16-bit or 8-bit label image column to each raw data input. To do this, you can use the node 'Annotate with data'. By default, JIPipe will ensure that all connected components of this image are assigned a unique component. You can disable this feature via the parameters. Does not support the training of image restoration models.

Troubleshooting

If you get blank outputs or poor segmentation after training:
  • Ensure you are starting from cpsam, not a custom or previously fine-tuned model
  • Verify that your label images have enough masks per image (minimum 5 by default)
  • Check that the learning rate is 1e-5 — higher values can destroy the pre-trained weights
  • Ensure training images have a similar diameter distribution to what you expect at inference time

external-imagej-macro:
Runs a custom ImageJ macro. JIPipe will iterate through the iteration steps and execute operations to convert JIPipe data into their ImageJ equivalent (see JIPipe to ImageJ parameter). Then the macro code is executed, followed by operations to import the result data into JIPipe data (see ImageJ to JIPipe parameter). Please feel free to click the 'Load example' button in the parameters to get started. Please keep in mind the following remarks:
  • Input images are opened as windows named according to the input slot. You have to select windows with the select() function or comparable functions.
  • Output images are extracted by finding a window that is named according to the output slot. Ensure to rename() windows accordingly.
  • To extract the 'Results' table output, add an output of type 'Results table' and set the name to 'Results'. Alternatively, you can configure the output in 'JIPipe to ImageJ' and override the name to 'Results'
  • To import other tables, use a different slot name or set the appropriate configuration.
  • Please note that there is only one ROI manager. This is a restriction of ImageJ.
  • Annotations can also be accessed via a function getJIPipeAnnotation(key), which returns the string value of the annotation or an empty string if no value was set.
  • You can define variables that are passed from JIPipe to ImageJ. Variables are also created for incoming path-like data, named according to the slot name.

Measures all components in the filament graph. Produces the following measurements:
  • number of vertices
  • number of edges
  • length (sum of edge lengths)
  • skeletonization-corrected length (adding 2 * radius for each vertex with degree 0 and 1 x radius for each vertex with degree 1)
  • confinement ratio (length of the simplified graph divided by the length)
  • number of vertices with specific degrees
  • min/max centroid x/y/z (per vertex) center[min/max][x/y/z]
  • min/max x/y/z (with sphere radius) sphere[min/max][x/y/z]
  • centroid x/y/z/c/t
  • min/max/avg radius/value
You can learn more about the generated measurements here: https://jipipe.hki-jena.de/documentation/filament-measurements.html

filaments-tsoax: TSOAX is an open source software to extract and track the growth and deformation of biopolymer networks from 2D and 3D time-lapse sequences. It tracks each filament or network branch from complex network dynamics and works well even if filaments disappear or reappear. The output is a set of tracks for each evolving filament or network segment.  TSOAX is an extension of SOAX (for network extraction in static images) to network extraction and tracking in time lapse movies.  TSOAX facilitates quantitative analysis of network dynamics of multi-dimensional biopolymer networks imaged by various microscopic imaging modalities. The underlying methods of TSOAX includes multiple Stretching Open Active Contour Models for extraction and a combined local and global graph matching framework to establish temporal correspondence among all extracted structures.

file-temporary: Generates a temporary file that will be located within your operating system's temporary directory or the directory specified in the JIPipe settings. Please note that there are no guarantees on the actual file name, as the outcome depends on the operating system.
folder-annotate-by-name: Creates an annotation for each path based on its name
folder-list-files: Takes each input folder and outputs the files it contains, optionally from a named subfolder and, if enabled, from all subfolders. A filter expression can keep only matching files, and recursive search can follow symbolic links.
folder-list-subfolders: Takes folders and lists the subfolders inside each one, optionally starting from a named subfolder and searching recursively. It can keep only folders matching filter conditions. The result is a list of folders for downstream steps.
folder-mkdir: Creates directories in the filesystem according to the input paths. If the path already exists, it will be silently skipped.
folder-run-output: Generates a path that points to the data output folder of the current run.
folder-temporary: Generates a temporary folder that will be located within your operating system's temporary directory or the directory specified in the JIPipe settings. Please note that there are no guarantees on the actual folder name, as the outcome depends on the operating system. The folder is already existing, so a 'Create directories' operation is not needed.
form-processor-iterating: An algorithm that iterates through groups of data in its 'Data' slot and shows a user interface during the runtime that allows users to modify annotations via form elements. Groups are based on the annotations. These forms are provided via the 'Forms' slot, where all contained form elements are shown in the user interface.After the user input, the form data objects are stored in an output slot (one set of copies per iteration step).
form-processor-merging: An algorithm that iterates through groups of data in its 'Data' slot and shows a user interface during the runtime that allows users to modify annotations via form elements. Groups are based on the annotations. These forms are provided via the 'Forms' slot, where all contained form elements are shown in the user interface.After the user input, the form data objects are stored in an output slot (one set of copies per iteration step).
form-processor-simple-iterating: An algorithm that iterates through each row of its 'Data' slot and shows a user interface during the runtime that allows users to modify annotations via form elements. These forms are provided via the 'Forms' slot, where all contained form elements are shown in the user interface. After the user input, the form data objects are stored in an output slot (one set of copies per iteration step).
generate-placeholder-for-missing-data: Creates a iteration step of the reference and data inputs. If the data is missing for a reference, it is extracted from the items in the placeholder slot.
generate-unique-annotation: Generates a unique annotation for each row based on its index. The annotations will have the format (Base name)[(row index)]
generate-unique-random-annotation: Generates a unique random numeric annotation. The value range is [0, number of rows]. This is useful for randomly distributing data.
get-exported-path: Generates an export path for the input data and returns it as JIPipe path data
graph-annotation-arrow: A canvas note that displays an arrow
graph-annotation-image: Places a static image box on the workflow canvas; it receives no data and outputs no data. It displays a selected image with configurable fit, anchor, scale, margins, background, and border.
graph-annotation-text-box: A canvas note that contains text
graph-wrapper:input: Marks the entry point of a grouped set of analysis steps. It takes no specific data type and produces no separate result; it simply lets the data you connect to the group enter unchanged for the steps inside to use.
graph-wrapper:output: It makes the final result of a node group available to the rest of the workflow. It takes that result from the grouped steps and passes it on without changing it.
group-header-form: Creates a group header element to structure the form.
group-scene-3d: Puts the objects in the incoming 3D scene into a group
ij-convert-image: Converts an image into another image type
ij-convert-image-to-16-bit-ij-auto-contr: Converts an image into 16-bit while applying ImageJ's automatic contrast functions per slice.
ij-convert-image-to-32-bit: Takes a 2D or 3D ImageJ image and produces a 32-bit grayscale image, where each pixel or voxel is stored as a 32-bit floating-point value. This is useful when later analysis needs more numeric precision than standard 8-bit or 16-bit images.
ij-convert-image-to-8-bit: Produces an 8-bit grayscale ImageJ image by converting the input 2D or 3D ImageJ image to 8-bit, with intensity values from 0 to 255.
ij-convert-image-to-8-bit-ij-auto-contra: Converts an image into 8-bit while applying ImageJ's automatic contrast functions per slice.
ij-convert-image-to-hsb-colors: Converts an image into HSB colors
ij-convert-image-to-lab-colors: Converts an image into LAB colors
ij-convert-image-to-rgb-colors: Takes a 2D or 3D image and converts it to RGB color data, producing an image whose pixels are represented as red, green, and blue channels. This makes the image suitable for steps that expect RGB color input.
ij-export-to-imagej: Runs an ImageJ exporter. You can select the utilized exporter type in the parameters.
ij-form-draw-mask: Allows users to draw or modify a mask that is drawn over a reference image. You can supply existing masks via the 'Masks' input. If a iteration step has no existing mask, a new one is generated according to the node parameters.
ij-form-draw-rois: Allows users to draw or modify ROIs that are drawn over a reference image. You can supply existing masks via the 'ROI' input. If a iteration step has no existing mask, a new one is generated according to the node parameters. BROKEN! USE THE MASK DRAWER INSTEAD OR USE IMAGEJ DIRECTLY!
ij-imgplus-from-gui: Imports one or multiple active ImageJ image windows into JIPipe
ij-imgplus-from-matrix: Creates an image from a matrix
ij-imgplus-to-gui: Opens all incoming images in ImageJ
ij-import-from-imagej: Runs an ImageJ importer. You can select the utilized importer type in the parameters.
ij-import-stack: Loads an image stack via the native ImageJ functions. The current implementation only allows 2D images to be imported and will show an error if higher-dimensional data is provided.
ij-math-chamfer-distance-map-2d: Computes the distance map from a binary image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij-math-chamfer-distance-map-3d: Computes the distance map from a binary image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij-math-geodesic-distance-map-2d: Computes the geodesic distance map from a binary image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij-math-label-chamfer-distance-map-3d: Computes the distance map from a label image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij-multi-template-matching: Template matching is an algorithm that can be used for object-detections in grayscale images. To perform template matching you will need a template image that is searched in the target image. The best is to simply crop a typical region of interest from a representative image.    The algorithm computes the probability to find one (or several) template images provided by the user into a larger image. The algorithm uses the template image as a sliding window translated over the image, and at each position of the template computes a similarity score between the template and the image patch. This results in a correlation map, for which the pixel value at position (x,y) is proportional to the similarity between the template and image patch, at this (x,y) position in the image. The computation of the correlation map is followed by extrema detection to list the possible locations of the template in the image. Each extrema corresponds to the possible location of a bounding box of dimensions identical to the template. The extrema detection can list a large number of extrema in the first place. Usually a threshold on the score is then used to limit this number (i.e. returning local extrema with a score above/below the threshold). To prevent overlapping detection of the same object, Non-Maxima Supression is performed after extrema detection.    Please visit https://github.com/multi-template-matching/MultiTemplateMatching-Fiji/wiki for more information about the Multi-Template Matching plugin.
ij-optical-flow-mse-block-flow: Transfers image sequences into an optic flow field. Flow fields are calculated for each pair (t,t+1) of the sequence with length |T| independently. The motion vector for each pixel in image t is estimated by searching the most similar looking pixel in image t+1. The similarity measure is the sum of square differences of all pixels in a local vicinity. The local vicinity is defined by a block and is calculated using an IntegralImage. Both the size of the block and the search radius are parameters of the method.  The output is a two-channel image with (T-1) items. The pixels in each channel describe the relative location of the next similar pixel in polar coordinates (default) or cartesian coordinates.
ij-optical-flow-mse-gaussian-flow: Transfers image sequences into an optic flow field. Flow fields are calculated for each pair (t,t+1) of the sequence with length |T| independently. The motion vector for each pixel in image t is estimated by searching the most similar looking pixel in image t+1. The similarity measure is the sum of differences of all pixels in a local vicinity. The local vicinity is defined by a Gaussian. Both the standard deviation of the Gaussian (the size of the local vicinity) and the search radius are parameters of the method.  The output is a two-channel image with (T-1) items. The pixels in each channel describe the relative location of the next similar pixel in polar coordinates (default) or cartesian coordinates.
ij-optical-flow-pmcc-block-flow: Transfers image sequences into an optic flow field. Flow fields are calculated for each pair (t,t+1) of the sequence with length |T| independently. The motion vector for each pixel in image t is estimated by searching the most similar looking pixel in image t+1. The similarity measure is Pearson Product-Moment Correlation Coefficient of all pixels in a local vicinity. The local vicinity is defined by a block and is calculated using an IntegralImage. Both the size of the block and the search radius are parameters of the method.  The output is a two-channel image with (T-1) items. The pixels in each channel describe the relative location of the next similar pixel in polar coordinates (default) or cartesian coordinates.
ij-results-table-from-gui: Imports one or multiple active ImageJ results table windows into JIPipe
ij-results-table-to-gui: Opens all incoming tables in ImageJ
ij-roi-from-gui: Imports ROI from the ImageJ ROI manager
ij-roi-to-gui: Adds all incoming ROI into the ImageJ ROI manager
ij1-analyze-annotate-by-image-statistics: Annotates the incoming images by their statistics. The statistics are created via annotations.
ij1-analyze-find-particles2d: Converts mask images into ROI by applying a connected components algorithm and generates measurements. Please note that this algorithm will always trace the external object boundaries and convert them into polygonal ROIs. This means that holes will be closed. This node requires a thresholded image as input and will extract measurements from the thresholded image. If you already have ROI available and want measurements, use 'Extract ROI statistics'.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the results are generated for each 2D slice.
ij1-analyze-image-statistics: Extracts statistics of the whole image or a masked part. Please note that this node will not be able to extract the shape of masked areas. All shape-description features (Centroid, Perimeter, ...) are calculated on the rectangle formed by the image dimensions.
ij1-analyze-image-statistics-expression: Extracts statistics of the whole image or a masked part. The table columns are created via expressions.
ij1-analyze-orientationj-vector-field-2d: Applies the OrientationJ vector field calculation algorithm
ij1-analyze-skeleton-2d3d: Tags all pixel/voxels in a skeleton image and then counts all its junctions, triple and quadruple points and branches, and measures their average and maximum length.
ij1-analyze-statistics-histogram: Generates a histogram of the input image. It generates following output columns: value, count.
ij1-analyze-statistics-histogram-key-val: This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and integrated, thus allowing to generate histograms. Allows the generation of normalized and cumulative histograms.
ij1-analyze-statistics-key-value-avg: This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. Buckets the pixels of the 'Value' image based on the pixel in the 'Key' and calculates the number of values, their sum, and the average value.
ij1-analyze-statistics-threshold-partiti: This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The set of value pixels is partitioned into two sets based on whether the key is lower, or equal/higher than the currently processed key. One or multiple values can be created for each partitioning.

This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The set of value pixels is partitioned into two sets based on whether the key is lower, or equal/higher than the currently processed key. This is a fast version of 'Key/Value threshold statistics 5D' that only produces the number of pixels in each partition, the sum of values, as well as the average.
ij1-analyze-statistics-threshold-value: This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and then integrated for each threshold in the key image.
ij1-analyze-statistics-threshold-value-f: This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and then integrated for each threshold in the key image. This variant uses table column integration functions that are faster than expression-based operations.

This node consumes two images with the same dimensions that respectively contain the keys and value components of each pixel position. The values assigned to each key are collected and then integrated for each threshold in the key image. This variant is hardcoded to calculate the average of the pixels per threshold.
ij1-apply-lut: Applies the currently set LUT of an image and converts the image to an RGB image. To modify the LUT,  please use one of the 'Set LUT' nodes.
ij1-background-rollingball2d: Finds or subtracts the background of a 2D slice via a rolling-ball or paraboloid algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-binary-binarize: Converts a greyscale image into a binary image. All pixels with a value larger than zero are set to 255.
ij1-binary-bitwise: Combines two 8-bit images with a bitwise operation. You can use it to, for example combine two masks.
ij1-binary-conditional-invert: Inverts the image if a condition (based on statistics) is met. Otherwise, the image is not inverted.
ij1-binary-connected-component-labeling-: Applies a connected components labeling on a mask. Each connected component is assigned a unique value in the output label image. If the image is non-binary, the connected components are generated per-input value. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.

Applies a connected components labeling on a mask. Each connected component is assigned a unique value in the output label image. If the image is non-binary, the connected components are generated per-input value. If 3D data is supplied, the connected components are extracted in 3D.
ij1-binary-convexify: Converts a 2D mask image into its convex hull. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-binary-dtwatershed2d: Applies an euclidean distance transform on binary images. Then applies a watershed algorithm.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-binary-hough-line-segments: Finds lines within the image via a Hough lines transformation. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-binary-hough-lines: Finds lines within the image via a Hough lines transformation. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. Please note that this node will not find line segments, but finds global linear structures. Legacy implementation based on code by David Chatting. We recommend to use the non-legacy algorithm for better results.
ij1-binary-hough-lines-global: Finds global lines within the image via a Hough lines transformation. Uses a similar algorithm to 'Detect line segments 2D (Hough)' with fill size infinite, but ensures that the resulting lines are starting and ending at the image borders. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-binary-keep-largest-region: Keeps only the largest connected component in the input mask.
ij1-binary-remove-largest-region: Keeps only the largest connected component in the input mask.
ij1-binary-uep2d: Find the maxima of the Euclidean distance transform. In the output, the points are assigned the EDM value, which is equal to the radius of the largest circle that fits into the particle, with the UEP as the center. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-binary-volume-opening-2d: Removes all objects with an area smaller than the provided number of pixels. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-binary-volume-opening-3d: Removes all objects with an area smaller than the provided number of pixels.
ij1-binary-voronoi2d: Splits the image by lines of points having equal distance to the borders of the two nearest particles.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-blur-box2d: Applies a 3x3 smoothing filter. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-blur-box2d-v2: Applies a box (local average) filter. Unlike local mean, this filter uses a filter kernel where all pixels have the same weight. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-blur-box3d: Applies convolution with a local mean function in 3D space for smoothing. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 3D slice.
ij1-blur-gaussian2d: Applies convolution with a Gaussian function for smoothing. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-blur-gaussian3d: Applies convolution with a Gaussian function in 3D space for smoothing. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 3D slice.
ij1-blur-median2d: Applies a median filter. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-blur-median2d-8u: Applies a 3x3 median filter to 8-bit greyscale images. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-blur-median2d-rgb: Applies a 3x3 median filter to RGB color images. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-blur-median3d: Applies convolution with a local median function in 3D space for smoothing. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 3D slice.
ij1-calibration-copy-physical-dimensions: Copies the phyiscal pixel sizes from the source to the target
ij1-calibration-draw-scale-bar: Draws a scale bar onto the image (via an overlay ROI)
ij1-calibration-set-physical-dimensions: Allows to set the physical dimensions of the incoming images
ij1-calibration-set-physical-dimensions-: Allows to set the physical dimensions of the incoming images. This node allows extracts the properties from the annotations.
Allows to set the physical dimensions of the incoming images. This node allows to utilize expressions that have access to annotations and image properties.
ij1-colocalization-coloc2: Colocalization analysis via the pixel intensity correlation over space methods of Pearson, Manders, Costes, Li and more, for scatterplots, analysis, automatic thresholding and statistical significance testing. Coloc 2 does NOT perform object based colocalization measurements, where objects are first segmented from the image, then their spatial relationships like overlap etc. are measured. This complementary approach is implemented in many ways elsewhere.
ij1-color-arrange-channels: Reorders the channels of each input image
ij1-color-blend-images: Takes one or more same-size greyscale or RGB images and combines them into one RGB image by overlaying them in priority order with chosen blend modes and opacities.
ij1-color-combine-rgb: If the input image has 3 channel axis slices, those channels are merged into one RGB slice. Useful if you imported images via Bio-Formats or other importers that automatically split channels.
ij1-color-convert-to-hsb: Converts an image into an HSB image or re-interprets existing image channels as HSB. Please note that this node is designed for color images.
ij1-color-convert-to-lab: Converts an image into an LAB image or re-interprets existing image channels as LAB. Please note that this node is designed for color images.
ij1-color-convert-to-rgb: Converts an image into an RGB image or re-interprets existing image channels as RGB. Please note that this node is designed for color images. Use 'Render to RGB'/'Convert image to RGB colors (Render)' if you have issues.
ij1-color-invert: Inverts the colors/values p of an image. With 8-bit images, p=255-p. With RGB images, converts each pixel to three 8-bit pixels and uses p=255-p. With 16-bit images, p=65535-p, or p=255-p, p=1024-p, etc. if an "Unsigned 16-bit range" is set using the "Set" option of the Image>Adjust>Brightness/ Contrast dialog. With 32-bit images, p=max-(p-min), where 'min' and 'max' are the minimum and maximum displayed pixel values.
ij1-color-invert-greyscale: Inverts the values p of an image. With 8-bit images, p=255-p. With 16-bit images, p=65535-p, or p=255-p, p=1024-p, etc. if an "Unsigned 16-bit range" is set using the "Set" option of the Image>Adjust>Brightness/ Contrast dialog. With 32-bit images, p=max-(p-min), where 'min' and 'max' are the minimum and maximum displayed pixel values.
ij1-color-invert-rgb: Inverts the colors by subtracting 255 from each RGB color channel.
ij1-color-merge-channels: Merges each greyscale image plane into a multi-channel image. Implements the standard ImageJ algorithm for merging channels that either creates an RGB or a composite image. We recommend to use Blend images for creating renders and Merge channels (composite) that provide more options for the specific use cases.
ij1-color-merge-channels-composite: Merges each greyscale image plane into a multi-channel image. Implements the standard ImageJ algorithm for merging channels that either creates an RGB or a composite image. We recommend to use Blend images for creating renders and Merge channels (composite) that provide more options for the specific use cases.
ij1-color-merge-channels-hsb: Merges three greyscale images into one HSB image.
ij1-color-merge-channels-lab: Merges three greyscale images into one LAB image.
ij1-color-merge-channels-rgb: Merges three greyscale images into one RGB image.
ij1-color-overlay-channels: Creates a composite image by merging channels of the inputs. Behaves similar to the ImageJ channel merger with composite setting, but with custom colors. Please note that the channels will be merged in order of the input slots.
ij1-color-set-to-color: Sets all pixels of the input image to the specified color. If the image is grayscale, the provided color is converted to its equivalent grayscale value.
ij1-color-set-to-content-aware-2d: Sets pixels of the input image inside the masked area to a generated value. Please review the 'Methods' parameter to find out more about the methods.
ij1-color-set-to-grayscale-value: Sets all pixels of the input image to the specified grayscale value. If the image is RGB, the value is converted into an integer that is parsed as RGB.
ij1-color-split-channels: Splits multichannel images into multiple greyscale images. This operation is applied for each 2D image slice.
ij1-color-split-channels-2: Splits multichannel images into multiple greyscale images. This operation is applied for each 2D image slice.
ij1-color-split-channels-by-table: Splits multichannel images into multiple greyscale images. This operation is applied for each 2D image slice. This node uses a reference table as secondary input that matches data to a channel assignment configuration. To configure this node, setup the set of annotation columns and the set of channel columns. The channel columns must be named according to the real (not labelled!) output slot name.
ij1-color-split-rgb: Split each RGB image channel into its own plane which will be put into the 'Channel' axis.
ij1-color-to-greyscale-expression: Applies a mathematical operation to each pixel to convert the color into a greyscale value.
ij1-color-to-rgb: Converts the incoming image to RGB. This applies the LUT if any is set. Compared to the image converter node, this operation renders the image into a representation equivalent to an image viewer, meaning that contrast settings are preserved.
ij1-contrast-apply-displayed-contrast: Applies the displayed contrast settings of the image and writes them into the pixel values. Does nothing if the image is a 32-bit floating point image. The operation is applied to all slices.
ij1-contrast-apply-ij-per-slice: Applies the ImageJ contrast enhancer per slice (writing the pixel values). Applies optional histogram stretching.
ij1-contrast-calibrate: Re-calibrates the incoming image, so its color range is displayed differently by ImageJ. This does not change the pixel data. Please note that the displayed contrast is stored into the image itself. If you want to convert to 8-bit or 16-bit where the contrast is applied per slice, use 'Convert image to 8-bit (ImageJ auto-contrast)' or 'Convert image to 16-bit (ImageJ auto-contrast)'. If you want to do the same for 32-bit images, use 'Apply ImageJ auto-contrast per slice'
ij1-contrast-clahe: Applies 'Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization' (CLAHE) to enhance contrast. Composite color images are converted into their luminance. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the results are generated for each 2D slice.
ij1-contrast-histogram-enhancer: Implementation of the ImageJ contrast enhancer feature that uses histograms and normalization methods.
ij1-contrast-illumination-correction2d: Applies a Gaussian filter to the image and extracts the maximum value. Pixel values are then divided by this value.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-convert-image-to-matrix: Extracts the pixel values of an image and puts them into a table in form of a matrix.
ij1-convert-image-to-table: Extracts the pixel values of an image and puts them into a table. The table always includes columns x, y, z, c, and t. For greyscale images, the value is stored into a column value. For color images, column names depend on the color space.
ij1-convert-image-to-table-column: Copies the first column of an image into a new or existing column of a table. Opposite operation to 'Table column to image'.
ij1-convert-matrix-to-image: Converts a table that represents a matrix into an image. The matrix can contain color values (HEX colors) if a color image is requested.
ij1-convert-multiple-images-to-table: Extracts the pixel values of multiple images and puts them into a table. The table always includes columns x, y, z, c, and t. For greyscale images, the value is stored into a column named according to the input. For color images, column names depend on the color space and are named SLOT_NAME.COLOR_CHANNEL.
ij1-convert-table-column-to-image: Converts a selected numeric table column into an image with 1px width and a height based on the number of rows. Opposite operation to 'Image to table column'.
ij1-convert-table-to-image: Converts a table of pixel information into an image
ij1-convolve-convolve2d-parameter: Applies a convolution with a user-defined filter kernel. The kernel is defined by a parameter.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. For the most precise results, we recommend to convert the image to 32-bit before applying a convolution. Otherwise ImageJ will apply conversion from and to 32-bit images itself, which can have unexpected results.
ij1-convolve-convolve2d-slot: Applies a convolution with a user-defined filter kernel. The kernel is defined by a second parameter slot.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. For the most precise results, we recommend to convert the image to 32-bit before applying a convolution. Otherwise ImageJ will apply conversion from and to 32-bit images itself, which can have unexpected results.
ij1-data-to-preview: Converts any data into preview image. Does not generate a result if no previews are supported.
ij1-dimensions-expression-slicer: Uses expressions to create custom stacks. There are three expressions, one for each Z, channel and frame plane that return numeric indices of slices that should be generated. You can optionally enable to iterate over all incoming slices of the image to generate multiple stacks. If no iteration is enabled (default), each expression is only executed for z=0,c=0,t=0.
ij1-dimensions-extended-depth-of-focus: Performs a Z, C, or T-Projection that selects the best-scoring pixel from the Z/C/T column. If no score image is provided, an automatically generated score is generated by either applying Sobel filter (Tenengrad), or by calculating the local variance. The resulting automatically generated score is then blurred using a Gaussian blur.
ij1-dimensions-hyper-stackslicer: Slices a hyperstack via a range of indices.
ij1-dimensions-hyper-stacksplitter: Splits a hyperstack by a selected dimension into a single or multiple output slots. Multiple output slots can be utilized to split specific indices.
ij1-dimensions-inpput2montage: Creates a montage of all 2D input images. The montage labels can be generated by available annotations. This node is deprecated. Use the node 'Create montage'.
ij1-dimensions-input2montage-v2: Creates a montage of all input images. Supports 2D and 3D images.
ij1-dimensions-merge-2d-to-hyperstack: Merges all incoming 2D slices into a hyperstack. The slice positions within the hyperstack can be controlled via expressions. The node can handle missing and negative slice positions due to a remapping procedure. Please ensure that there are no duplicate locations.
ij1-dimensions-montage2stack: Slices an image montage into a stack.
ij1-dimensions-reorder: Reorders dimensions of hyperstacks. This for example allows you to switch the depth and time axis. If a stack is provided, it is interpreted as hyperstack with depth and with one frame and one channel. 2D images are ignored and passed to the output without processing.
ij1-dimensions-reorder-hyperstack-slices: Uses an expression that iterates through all hyperstack slices to assign a new location within the output hyperstack. Can also filter slices based on the location.
ij1-dimensions-reslice: Defines a new Z axis and projects the image so that its Z axis is the newly defined one.
ij1-dimensions-stack-combine: Combines the incoming stacks into one by adding the corresponding slices of the second stack to the first one. For example, this allows to combine two one-channel stacks with the same number of slices into one with two channels. This node has similar functionality to the 'Merge stacks into dimension' node.
ij1-dimensions-stack-to-2d: Splits high-dimensional image stacks into 2D planes
ij1-dimensions-stack2montage: Converts an image stack into a montage. Deprecated. Use the algorithm with the same name.
ij1-dimensions-stack2montage-v2: Converts an image stack into a montage.
ij1-dimensions-stackinverter: Inverts the order of a Z-stack.
ij1-dimensions-stackmerger: Merges 2D image planes into a 3D stack. Data annotations are used to put images into groups. All images in a group are then merged into a 3D stack. The order of the stack slices is determined by the 'Slice index annotation' that is ignored while defining the groups.
ij1-dimensions-stacks-to-dimension: Merges multiple stacks that miss a dimension into the target dimension. Requires that all incoming stacks have the same size and that there is only one slice in the created dimension. The type of the output image is determined by consensus bit depth. This node has similar functionality to the 'Combine stacks' node.
ij1-dimensions-stacks-to-dimension-2: Merges multiple stacks that miss a dimension into the target dimension. Requires that all incoming stacks have the same size and that there is only one slice in the created dimension. The type of the output image is determined by the consensus bit depth. This node has similar functionality to the 'Combine stacks' node. If no order (ascending) is given for each input, the order of input images is determined by the order in the slot list.
ij1-dimensions-stacksplitter: Splits incoming stacks into a customizable amount of stacks based on stack indices. Add more output slots to create more groups. Please note that this node utilizes slice indices and cannot handle 5D images. Please use 'Reduce & split hyperstack' or 'Reduce & split hyperstack (Expression)' if you want to properly handle 5D images.
ij1-dimensions-zproject: Performs a Z-Projection. This version of the Z-project algorithm wraps around the native ImageJ function and can only handle 3D images. If you have a hyperstack (4D+), use the other Z-project algorithm.
ij1-dimensions-zproject-2: Performs a Z-Projection. Also supports other axes C-Project/T-Project.
ij1-edge-canny: Applies a Canny edge detector. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-edge-laplacian: Applies a Laplacian operator. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-edge-sobel: Applies a Sobel edge detector. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-enhance-bleach-correction: Applies bleach correction for 2D or 3D time series. Applies bleach correction per channel.
ij1-export-ome-zarr: Takes 2D or 3D OME image data and writes each as an OME-ZARR dataset in a folder or ZIP file, then outputs a URI reference to the result. It can create a multi-resolution pyramid, select compression, and define chunk sizes.
ij1-extract-ome-image-roi: Extracts the ROI from an OME image
ij1-extract-ome-image-xml: Extracts the OME metadata from an OME image and outputs it as OME-XML data. It takes an OME image and produces the XML that describes its channels, sizes, and acquisition metadata.
ij1-feature-difference-of-gaussian: Applies Gaussian blur to the input image twice with different sigma values resulting in two images which are then subtracted from each other. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-feature-directional-filter-2d: Filter that enhances curvilinear structures by applying oriented filters, while preserving their thickness. More information: https://imagej.net/plugins/morpholibj. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-feature-featurej-derivatives: Multi-dimensional, Gaussian-scaled derivatives of images, which form the basis of differential-geometric descriptions of image features found in literature on human and computer vision. The differentiation operation is carried out for each time frame and channel in a 5D image.Derivative images are obtained by separable convolution with derivatives of the multi-dimensional Gaussian function. This necessarily involves sampling and truncation of the continuous Gaussian function. At very small smoothing scales (less than about half the derivative order), this causes sampling artifacts, whereas at very large scales (where the kernel would have to be larger than twice the image size in the corresponding dimension), this causes truncation artifacts. In both cases, the sampled convolution kernel does not faithfully represent the shape of the original continuous function (due to undersampling or truncation), and the results become meaningless. The algorithm uses mirror-boundary conditions to obtain values outside the image at (positions close to) the boundaries.
ij1-feature-featurej-hessian: Computes Hessian the eigenvalues of the Hessian, which can be used for example to discriminate locally between plate-like, line-like, and blob-like image structures. All largest eigenvalues are put in a separate image, as are all smallest, and in 3D all middle as well. If the size of the image is unity in the z-dimension (single slice), the node computes 2D-Hessian eigenvalues, otherwise it computes 3D-Hessian eigenvalues (for each time frame and channel in a 5D image).
ij1-feature-featurej-structure: Computes for each image element (pixel/voxel) the eigenvalues of the so-called structure tensor, which can be used for example in texture analysis and image enhancement filtering. Due to the positive-semi-definiteness of the structure tensor, the eigenvalues are always larger than or equal to zero. If the size of the image is unity in the z-dimension (single slice), the node computes 2D-tensor eigenvalues, otherwise it computes 3D-tensor eigenvalues (for each time frame and channel in a 5D image).
ij1-feature-harris-corner-2d: OrientationJ implementation of the the Harris corner detection.
ij1-feature-laplacian-of-gaussian: Applies a Laplacian of Gaussian filter. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-feature-maxima-local-2d: Finds the local maxima of each image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-feature-mfc-2d: Calculates the Morphological Feature Contrast (MFC) of the image. For upper MFC, applies the following transformation to the input image f: MFC+ = MAX(0, f - Opening(r2, Closing(r1, f))). For lower MFC, applies the following transformation to the input image f: MFC- = MAX(0, Closing(r2, Opening(r1, f)) - f). For the full MFC, applies the following transformation to the input image f: MFC = MFC+ + MFC-. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-feature-mtc-2d: Calculates the Morphological Texture Contrast (MTC) of the image. Applies the following transformation to the input image f: MTC = MAX(0, Opening(r2, Closing(r1, f)) - Closing(r2, Opening(r1, f))). If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-feature-orientationj-2d: Extracts various orientation-related features from the input image. These are the same features as produced by the OrientationJ Analysis.
ij1-feature-shadows-2d: Produces a shadows effect in the given direction
ij1-feature-vesselness-frangi: Applies the vesselness filter developed by Frangi et al.
ij1-fft-forward2d: Converts a real space image into an image in frequency space.
ij1-fft-inverse2d: Converts a frequency space image into an image in real space.
ij1-fft-swap2d: Swaps the quadrants of a frequency space image.
ij1-filter-kuwahara2d: Applies a Kuwahara filter, a noise-reduction filter that preserves edges. Also supports the linear Kuwahara algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-generate-filter-kernel: Generates a structure element that is consistent with the ones used by the 2D morphological operation.
ij1-generate-filter-kernel-3d: Generates a structure element that is consistent with the ones used by the 3D morphological operation.
ij1-generate-missing-results-table: Generates placeholder or empty tables for data that are not paired with a matching table in the same iteration step.
ij1-generate-missing-results-table-2: Generates placeholder or empty tables for data that are not paired with a matching table in the same iteration step.
ij1-generate-zero-image: Creates a new blank ImageJ image filled with zero intensity, using the selected width, height, Z, C, and T sizes and pixel type (default 8-bit grayscale). It needs no input image, although optional annotations can be supplied, and outputs the generated image.
ij1-image-extract-metadata: Extracts the metadata (properties map) of the image and writes them into a table
ij1-image-remove-metadata: Allows to filter/remove specific image metadata entries
ij1-image-set-metadata-from-table: Sets the image metadata (property map) from a table. Only the first row is utilized.
ij1-image-set-properties-from-expression: Sets properties of the input images to values extracted from expressions.
ij1-invert-lut: Inverts the current LUT. If no LUT is set, a white-to-black LUT is generated. This does not change the pixel data.
ij1-labels-annotate-with-overlap-statist:
Compares two label or binary images and calculates measurements of their overlap error or agreement. Measurements include:
  • Overlap
  • Jaccard index
  • Dice coefficient
  • Volume Similarity
  • False Negative Error
  • False Positive Error
ij1-labels-crop-labels: Crops all or a specific subset of labels from the image.
ij1-labels-dilate-labels: Applies a constrained dilation of labels without unwanted growing/shrinking bordering regions (dilation only over the background)
ij1-labels-expand-labels: Adds space between labels to make them more easily distinguishable
ij1-labels-extract-statistics: Extracts statistics for all labels in the image. Statistics are extracted over an image (optional). If no image is supplied, the label itself will be used as the image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-labels-filter-by-mask: Deletes or keeps labels by a mask image. If the mask is white (value larger than zero) on overlapping a pixel, the associated label is kept or deleted (depending on the setting)
ij1-labels-filter-by-overlap: Filters the labels by testing for mutual overlap. The Labels 1 output contains all Labels 1 input labels that overlap with any of Labels 2. The Labels 2 output contains all Labels 2 input labels that overlap with a Labels 1 Labels. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-labels-filter-by-statistics: Filters the ROI list elements via statistics. Statistics are extracted over an image (optional). If no image is supplied, the label itself will be used as the image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-labels-filter-filter-by-expression-2: Filters labels with a filter expression. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-labels-filter-filter-by-expression-3: Takes a 3D grayscale image of labeled objects and keeps only the labels that satisfy a user-written expression, such as id > 10 AND num_pixels > 50, then outputs the same 3D grayscale image with all other labels removed.
ij1-labels-filter-labels-by-id: Allows to keep only a specific set of labels.
ij1-labels-filter-labels-by-thickness: Filter labels by their thickness as estimated by a EDT per label
ij1-labels-get-label-boundaries: Creates a mask that is 255 at the boundary between two labels and background.
ij1-labels-merge-labels: Sets all labels inside the specified ROI to the same value.
ij1-labels-merge-labels-to-bins: Merges labels into a specified number of of bins. The values are distributed so uniformly unless 'Equalize frequencies' is enabled. The resulting labels are determined by the bin index.  If the image has multiple slices, the algorithm is applied per slice.
ij1-labels-merge-labels-to-thickness: Merges labels until the thickness of the label reaches a minimum threshold. If the image has multiple slices, the algorithm is applied per slice.
ij1-labels-merge-small-labels: Merges labels with a low number of pixels to its neighboring label set (larger or smaller).
ij1-labels-overlap-statistics:
Compares two label or binary images and calculates measurements of their overlap error or agreement. Measurements include:
  • Overlap
  • Jaccard index
  • Dice coefficient
  • Volume Similarity
  • False Negative Error
  • False Positive Error
ij1-labels-remap: Ensures that the labels in the given label image range from 1 to Lmax.
ij1-labels-remove-border-labels: Sets all labels to zero that are connected to the image borders.
ij1-labels-remove-largest-label: Remove the label with the largest area
ij1-labels-replace-labels: Replaces label values by the specified value.
ij1-labels-replace-labels-by-table: Replaces label values by a mapping as specified in a table. The table should contain two columns, one for the old label and a second column defining the replacement value.
ij1-labels-separate: Splits all labels from a labels image into their own image. Can be reverted with Image calculator 2D (merge).
ij1-labels-separate-touching-labels: Finds pixels that border two different label values and sets them to the background value. Background pixels (value 0) are ignored.
ij1-labels-split-connected-components-2d: Splits labels that have the same value, but are not in the same connected component. Please note that that all label values will be re-assigned.
ij1-labels-to-mask: Converts a grayscale label image into a binary mask image: every pixel with a positive label value becomes white (255), and all other pixels become black (0), preserving the original size, channels, and scale.
ij1-labels-to-rgb: Visualizes a labels image by assigning a color to each label component
ij1-labels-to-roi: Converts a label image into a set of ROI. Labels must have a value larger than zero to be detected.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. The Z/C/T coordinates of the source slices are saved inside the ROI.
ij1-math-compare-images-2d: Compares each pixel position and returns a 255 where the condition applies and 0 where the condition does not apply.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. 'Fast image arithmetics' covers the feature set of this node.
ij1-math-divide-by-maximum: Divides greyscale pixel values by the global maximum across all slices.
ij1-math-edt2d: Applies a euclidean distance transform on binary images.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-math-extended-maxima-2d: Returns the extended maxima. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-math-extended-minima-2d: Returns the extended minima. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-math-fast-image-arithmetics: Applies standard arithmetic and logical operations including, addition, subtraction, division, multiplication, GAMMA, EXP, LOG, SQR, SQRT, ABS, AND, OR, XOR, minimum, maximum, and more.
ij1-math-generate-from-expression: Applies a mathematical operation to each pixel. The value is written into the image.
ij1-math-generate-missing-from-expressio: Generates an image if it cannot be matched to a reference in a iteration step according to the mathematical operation. Applies a mathematical operation to each pixel. The value is written into the image.
ij1-math-generate-missing-zero-image: Generates an empty (black) image if it cannot be matched to a reference
ij1-math-generate-vector-from-expression: Generates a vector field by utilizing a math expression. The expression must return an array of numbers (or scalar if there are only 1 components).
ij1-math-hessian2d: Deprecated: Replace with node with the same name. ij1-math-local-mean3d: Calculates the local mean around each pixel. This is also referred as greyscale dilation. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 3D slice.
ij1-math-local-minimum2d: Calculates the local minimum around each pixel. This is also referred as greyscale erosion. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-math-local-minimum3d: Calculates the local minimum around each pixel. This is also referred as greyscale erosion. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 3D slice.
ij1-math-local-variance2d: Calculates the local variance around each pixel. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-math-local-variance3d: Calculates the local variance around each pixel. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 3D slice.
ij1-math-math2d: Applies a mathematical operation to each pixel. Supported operations are SET, ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, DIVIDE, GAMMA, MINIMUM, MAXIMUM, LOGICAL OR, LOGICAL AND, and LOGICAL XOR. We recommend to use 'Fast image arithmetics' instead.
ij1-math-math2d-expression: Applies a mathematical operation to each pixel. Please note that is node has a high computational cost. Check if you can replace it with 'Fast image arithmetics'.
ij1-math-math2d-expression-color: Applies a mathematical operation to each pixel. The three available channels can be addressed individually. Please note that is node has a high computational cost.
ij1-math-regional-maxima-2d: Returns the regions that have a constant intensity value and are surrounded by lower intensity values. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-math-regional-maxima-3d: Returns the regions that have a constant intensity value and are surrounded by higher intensity values.
ij1-math-regional-minima-2d: Returns the regions that have a constant intensity value and are surrounded by higher intensity values. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-math-regional-minima-3d: Returns the regions that have a constant intensity value and are surrounded by higher intensity values.
ij1-math-replace-nan-by-median2d: Filter that removes NaN values from floating point images by replacing them by the local median. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-math-round-32f: Rounds the values in a 32-bit image to a specific number of decimals
ij1-math-transform2d: Applies a mathematical function to each pixel. Supported operations are: ABS, INVERT, SQUARE, LOGARITHM, SQRT, and EXP
ij1-math-vector-expression: Applies a mathematical operation to each vector in the image. One dimension is defined as the dimension that contains the vector components. For example, you can make the channel the vector components. The algorithm then would iterate through all X, Y, Z, and T pixels and provide you with an array of all channel pixel values for this position. The output is a scalar image.
ij1-ml-labkit-segmentation: Uses Labkit to segment or calculate the probability map of the input images
ij1-morph-binary-fillholes2d: Applies a morphological hole filling operation to binary images.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-morph-binary-operation2d: Applies a morphological operation to binary images.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-morph-binary-outline2d: Applies a morphological outline operation (gradient) to binary images.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-morph-binary-skeletonize2d: Applies a morphological skeletonization operation to binary images.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-morph-binary-skeletonize3d: Performs the skeletonization of 2D and 3D binary images (8-bit images)
ij1-morph-find-holes-3d: Find holes by extracting the ROI located in the image and utilizing the fact that ROI cannot have holes. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-morph-grayscale-attribute-filtering-:
Attribute filters aim at removing components of an image based on a certain size criterion, rather than on intensity. The most common and useful criterion is the number of pixels/voxels (i.e., the area or volume). For example, a morphological size opening operation with a threshold value of 20 will remove all blobs containing fewer than 20 voxels. The length of the diagonal of the bounding box can also be of interest to discriminate elongated versus round component shapes.

Application to binary images

When applied to a binary image, attribute opening consists in identifying each connected component, computing the attribute measurement of each component, and retain only the connected components whose measurement is above a specified value. This kind of processing is often used to clean-up segmentation results.

Application to grayscale images

When applied to a grayscale image, attribute opening consists in generating a series of binary images by thresholding at each distinct gray level in the image. The binary attribute opening described above is then applied independently to each binary image and the grayscale output is computed as the union of the binary results. The final output is a grayscale image whose bright structures with the attribute below a given value have disappeared. A great advantage of this filter is that the contours of the structures area better preserved than opening with a structuring element. As for classical morphological filters, grayscale attribute closing or tophat can be defined. Grayscale attribute closing consists in removing dark connected components whose size is smaller than a specified value. White [resp. Black] Attribute Top-Hat considers the difference of the attribute opening [resp. closing] with the original image, and can help identifying bright [resp. dark] structures with small size.

ij1-morph-operation2d: Applies a morphological operation to greyscale images. ij1-morph-operation3d: Applies a morphological operation to greyscale images. Following operations are included: Erosion, Dilation, Opening, Closing, White Top Hat, Black Top Hat, Gradient, Laplacian, Internal Gradient, and External Gradient. More information (including examples) can be found at https://imagej.net/MorphoLibJ.html If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel.
ij1-morph-reconstruct-2d: Geodesic reconstruction repeats conditional dilations or erosions until idempotence. Two images are required: the marker image, used to initialize the reconstruction, an the mask image, used to constrain the reconstruction. More information: https://imagej.net/plugins/morpholibj
ij1-morph-reconstruct-3d: Geodesic reconstruction repeats conditional dilations or erosions until idempotence.
