ij1-noise-add-salt-and-pepper-noise2d: Adds salt and pepper noise to the image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-noise-addnormalnoise2d: Adds normal distributed noise with mean zero and customizable standard deviation to the image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-noise-despeckle2d: Applies a median filter with radius=1. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-noise-removeoutliers2d: Filter that replaces pixel values by the median if they deviate too much from it. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-overlay: Overlays the target image with the source image according to a mask or ROI.
ij1-remove-lut: Takes an ImageJ image (ImagePlusData) and produces an ImageJ image (ImagePlusData) with its lookup table (LUT) color mapping removed, leaving pixel values unchanged. By default it works on a duplicate, and you can restrict the removal to selected channels.
ij1-render-color-map: Creates a new image that renders the contents of a color map as RGB image.
ij1-roi-append-rectangles: Appends manually defines rectangular ROI to all input ROI lists. Ths algorithm allows to add rectangles as margins. As no reference image is available, the reference area is defined by the bounds of the already existing ROI.
ij1-roi-append-rectangles-referenced: Appends manually defines rectangular ROI to all input ROI lists. Ths algorithm allows to add rectangles as margins to the reference image bounds.
ij1-roi-assemble-from-roi: Assembles/overlays extracted ROI onto the target images.
ij1-roi-calculator: Applies logical operations to the input ROI list. The logical operations are applied to the whole list, meaning that an AND operation will create the union of all ROI in the list. If you want to apply the operation only to a sub-set of ROI, preprocess using a ROI splitter algorithm.
ij1-roi-color-by-name: Takes a list of 2D ROIs and returns the same list with each ROI's fill and/or line color set according to its name. Unique names are sorted naturally, and each name's position in that order is mapped through the selected color map(s).
ij1-roi-color-statistics: Sets the ROI item colors by measurements.
ij1-roi-combine: Merges multiple ROI lists. The ROI from 'Source' are added to the end of the 'Target' list. Compared to 'Merge ROI lists', this node allows to control the order of the operation.
ij1-roi-convert-to-table: Writes the point coordinates and other metadata of the incoming ROI into a table
ij1-roi-count: Outputs one table that contains the counts for each incoming ROI. Each ROI list produces one column in the output table and contains all annotations of the incoming ROI data. You can add multiple input slots. All output table column is named according to the slot name of the incoming ROI list.This node can merge ROI lists according to their annotations. The sum of the counts within the same iteration step are generated.
ij1-roi-crop-list: Moves all ROI in the list so that their bounding rectangle is located at x=0 and y=0 (default). Also allows to crop the channel, time, and Z locations.
ij1-roi-dimension-reorder: Reorders dimensions of all the ROI contained in the ROI lists. Unlike the equivalent method for images, this node allows to have non-unique mappings.
ij1-roi-draw-line: Draws one or multiple ROI that have two definition points, including lines, rectangles, and ovals.
ij1-roi-draw-oval: Draws one or multiple oval/ellipse ROI. We recommend to use the 'Draw 2D rectangle/oval/line ROI' algorithm.
ij1-roi-draw-rectangle: Draws one or multiple rectangular ROI. Also supports the drawing of rounded rectangles.  We recommend to use the 'Draw 2D rectangle/oval/line ROI' algorithm.
ij1-roi-draw-scalebar: Draws a scale bar ROI. Compared to 'Draw scale bar', this node allows better control over overlay.
ij1-roi-draw-text: Creates a 2D text ROI and adds it to an existing 2D ROI list, or starts a new list if none is provided. It positions the text relative to an optional reference image or the current ROI bounds, with font, angle, and optional background settings, and outputs the updated 2D ROI list.
ij1-roi-enlarge-shrink: Outputs a new list of 2D ROIs, each enlarged or shrunk by a user-defined number of pixels; negative values shrink. It takes a list of 2D ROIs and an optional reference image, and the value can be based on ROI measurements or metadata.
ij1-roi-explode: Splits the ROI in a ROI list into individual ROI lists.
ij1-roi-extract-from-roi: Extracts parts of the incoming image within the given ROI by extracting the bounding area.
ij1-roi-extract-metadata: Extracts the metadata (properties map) of each ROI and writes them into a table
ij1-roi-extract-profile: Extracts the pixel intensities along the ROI if a straight or irregular line ROI are given. If a rotated rectangle is processed, it is converted into a straight line.If any other ROI type is given, either the row or column average of the bounding rectangle is calculated.
ij1-roi-filter-and-merge-statistics-scri: Executes a script that has full control over the input ROI lists. The Python script contains a variable 'row_lists' that contains dictionaries with following entries: 'roi_list' is a list of dictionaries, 'annotations' is a dictionary containing the annotations. Each 'data' dictionary has an item 'data' containing the ImageJ ROI, and a dictionary 'stats' with the extracted statistics.
ij1-roi-filter-by-name: Filters the ROI list elements by the name and other basic properties.
ij1-roi-filter-by-overlap: Filters the ROI lists by testing for mutual overlap. The ROI1 output contains all ROI1 input ROI that overlap with any of ROI2. The ROI2 output contains all ROI2 input ROI that overlap with a ROI1 ROI. This node is deprecated and was replaced with 'Filter 2D ROI by overlap'.
ij1-roi-filter-by-overlap-v2: Only returns candidate ROIs that overlap with at least N ROIs from the filter set.
ij1-roi-filter-roi-lists: Only passes ROI lists that match the filter criteria.
ij1-roi-filter-slice: Extracts a sublist of ROI from the input
ij1-roi-filter-statistics: Keeps only 2D ROIs that match a user-defined expression based on their measured values. It takes a list of 2D ROIs and an optional reference image, calculates the selected measurements for each ROI, and outputs the remaining 2D ROIs.
ij1-roi-filter-statistics-script: Filters the ROI list elements via statistics. The Python script contains a variable 'roi_list' that contains dictionaries. Each one has an item 'data' containing the ImageJ ROI, and a dictionary 'stats' containing the statistics.
ij1-roi-flatten: Removes the Z/C/T coordinates of ROI. Equivalent to setting Z/C/T to zero.
ij1-roi-flood-fill: Starts a flood fill (magic wand) operation starting at the location of the ROI. Multiple operations are applied for each point within the ROI. Returns the generated outlines.
ij1-roi-from-mask: Converts pixel values equal or higher than the given threshold to a ROI. This will create a single ROI that contains holes. If a higher-dimensional image is provided, the operation is applied for each slice.
ij1-roi-from-rectangles-referenced: Manually defines a rectangular ROI. This algorithm requires a reference image, but also allows more flexibility in defining the rectangles.
ij1-roi-from-table-circle: Converts data from a table to circular ROIs. The ROIs are created to be centered at the provided locations. If you require more options, utilize 'Table to rectangular/oval ROIs' instead.
ij1-roi-from-table-line: Converts data from a table to line ROIs.
ij1-roi-from-table-point: Creates a list of 2D point ROIs from a results table, using one row per point. It reads X and Y coordinates (and optional Z, channel, frame, name, and JSON metadata) and outputs a 2D ROI list that can be overlaid on images.
ij1-roi-from-table-rectangular: Converts data from a table to rectangular or oval ROIs. This node provides more options than the 'Table to circular ROIs' node.
ij1-roi-from-table-text: Turns a results table of coordinates and labels into a list of 2D text ROIs, one per row, positioned by X and Y. It can also set text, name, metadata, slice, channel, and time, and an optional background, producing ROIs that can be overlaid on images.
ij1-roi-generate-missing: Generates empty ROI lists for data that are not paired with a matching ROI in the same iteration step.
ij1-roi-generate-name: Utilizes an expression to generate a ROI name for each individual ROI in the supplied ROI lists.The expression has access to annotations and statistics.
ij1-roi-get-image: Gets the associated image from a ROI. No output is generated if the ROI have no associated images.
ij1-roi-interpolate: Converts the ROI into a sub-pixel resolution ROI of floating-point coordinates spaced interval pixels apart.
ij1-roi-merge: Merges multiple ROI lists by using data annotations. By default, ROIs with equivalent annotations are put into the same group and merged into one ROI list for each group. Use the parameters to control how groups are created. To merge all incoming ROI lists into just one list, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave the list of annotation columns empty.
ij1-roi-merge-pairwise-or: Merges each individual ROI in Target with each individual ROI in Source, generating all pairwise combinations of all ROI.
ij1-roi-outline:
Applies one of the following operations to all ROI in the list:
  • Convert to closed polygon
  • Convert to polygon
  • Calculate convex hull
  • Convert to bounding rectangle
  • Convert to minimum bounding rectangle (rotated rectangle)
  • Convert to oriented line
  • Convert to fitted circle
  • Convert to fitted ellipse
  • Apply split fitting to polygons
ij1-roi-outline-concave-hull-moreira-san: Uses the algorithm by Moreira and Santos to calculate the concave hull of the provided rois
ij1-roi-process-copy-across-zct: Copies the ROIs within the input list across another C/Z/T dimension. For example, if a ROI only exists within one channel, and different ROIs are required for each channel, this node then can copy the ROIs to the other channel locations with a unique name. If you just want measurements across multiple channels, use 'Change 2D ROI properties' to set the channel location to zero, which yields a behavior consistent with ImageJ.
ij1-roi-register-max-brightness: Tests multiple locations of the specified ROI within the image and finds the scale, rotation, and translation of the ROI where its components align to the maximum average intensity.
ij1-roi-relation-2d: Extracts all pairwise statistics between the 2D ROI
ij1-roi-remove-bordering: Removes all ROI that intersect with image borders. Use the 'Border' parameter to define a rectangle inside of the image dimensions. If a ROI is not contained within this region, it is removed.
ij1-roi-remove-metadata: Allows to filter/remove specific ROI metadata entries
ij1-roi-remove-overlay: It takes an ImageJ image (ImagePlusData) and produces a copy (ImagePlusData) with the overlay removed, so any 2D ROI or 3D ROI markings are no longer displayed.
ij1-roi-render-overlay: Creates a color image in which the 2D ROIs from the input image's overlay are drawn over the image. It takes an ImagePlusData image and produces an ImagePlusColorRGBData image, applying the selected outline, fill, label, opacity, and magnification settings.
ij1-roi-rotate: Rotates all ROI in the ROI list. A newer algorithm that allows to do scaling/rotating/translation in one is available.
ij1-roi-scale: Scales all ROI in the ROI list. If you want to have more flexibility, use one of the 'Change ROI properties' nodes. A newer algorithm that allows to do scaling/rotating/translation in one is available.
ij1-roi-set-image: Associates an image to the ROI.
ij1-roi-set-metadata-from-table: Sets the ROI metadata (property map) from a table. The table either has a column that indicates the ROI index or contains one row per ROI (row index is the ROI index)
ij1-roi-set-overlay: Sets the overlay of an image to a supplied list of 2D ROIs, producing an image that carries those ROIs for display or further analysis. It takes an image and a 2D ROI list and outputs the same image with the overlay applied.
ij1-roi-set-properties: Sets properties of all Roi to a user-defined value.
ij1-roi-set-properties-from-annotation: Sets properties of all Roi to values extracted from annotations.
ij1-roi-set-properties-from-expressions: Sets properties of all ROI to values extracted from expressions.
ij1-roi-set-properties-from-table: Sets properties of all ROI to values extracted from a table. Table rows are matched to their ROI and the column values are put into expression variables, so the ROI can be modified.
ij1-roi-sort-and-extract-statistics: Sorts the ROI list elements via statistics and allows to you extract the n top values. Optionally, line and fill colors of the output rows can be colored according to the output order.
ij1-roi-sort-and-extract-statistics-2: Sorts the ROI list elements via statistics and allows to you extract the n top values. Optionally, line and fill colors of the output rows can be colored according to the output order.
ij1-roi-sort-by-statistics-expression: Sorts a ROI list according to an expression-defined property. Has access to annotations and measurements.
ij1-roi-split: Splits ROI that consist of multiple sub-ROI into their individual ROI. Such multi-component ROI are for example generated by the ROI calculator.
ij1-roi-split-by-statistics: Splits the incoming 2D ROI lists by a classifier value that is calculated based on statistics.
ij1-roi-split-into-connected-components: Algorithm that extracts connected components across one or multiple dimensions. The output consists of multiple ROI lists, one for each connected component.
ij1-roi-statistics: Generates a results table containing ROI statistics. If a reference image is provided, the statistics are calculated for the reference image. Otherwise, an empty reference image is automatically generated.
ij1-roi-to-annotations: Extracts properties of the ROI lists and stores them into annotations. This will create a list of annotation values if there are multiple ROI per list, unless you choose the option to only return the first entry. By default, one value per ROI is generated. Enable de-duplication to disable this behavior.
ij1-roi-to-centroid: Converts the ROI into point ROI that are the centroids of their inputs
ij1-roi-to-labels-expression: Converts ROI and an optional reference image into a label image. Each ROI is assigned its own label. Alternatively, the label can be set generated from an expression. If no reference image is provided, the dimensions are estimated from the ROI. The background color (where no ROI is located) is zero.
ij1-roi-to-labels-name: Converts ROI and an optional reference image into a label image. The label value is provided by mapping the name to a value. If no name mapping is provided for a ROI, a unique label is generated. If no reference image is provided, the dimensions are estimated from the ROI. The background color (where no ROI is located) is zero.
ij1-roi-to-mask: Converts ROI lists to masks. This algorithm needs a reference image that provides the output sizes. If you do not have a reference image, you can use the unreferenced variant.
ij1-roi-to-mask-unreferenced: Converts ROI lists to masks. This algorithm does not need a reference image that determines the output size.
ij1-roi-to-rgb: Creates an RGB image that draws 2D ROIs as colored outlines, fills, and optional labels. It takes a 2D ROI list and an optional reference image; without a reference, it uses a blank RGB canvas. The output is an RGB image of the ROI visualization.
ij1-roi-to-rgb-unreferenced: Converts ROI lists to color images. The line and fill color is stored within the ROI themselves. This algorithm does not need a reference image that determines the output size.
ij1-roi-transform-2d: Applies rotation, scaling, and translation of 2D ROI.
ij1-roi-unset-image: Removes any association of the ROI from any image.
ij1-segment-classic-watershed: Performs segmentation via watershed on a 2D or 3D image using flooding simulations. Please note that this node returns labels instead of masks.
ij1-segment-ridge-detector-2d: A ridge detector that detects lines and outputs a binary mask where lines are detected.
ij1-segment-seeded-watershed: Performs segmentation via watershed on a 2D or 3D image using flooding simulations. Please note that this node returns labels instead of masks. The markers need to be labels, so apply a connected components labeling if you only have masks.
ij1-set-lut-from-color-image: Sets the LUT of the image from another image, which should be a RGB image with a width of 256 and a height of 1. This does not change the pixel data.
ij1-set-lut-from-color-map: Sets the LUT of the image from a predefined color map. This does not change the pixel data.
ij1-set-lut-from-colors: Generates a LUT from the first to the second color. This does not change the pixel data.
ij1-sharpen-laplacian2d: Applies a 3x3 sharpening filter. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-simple-image-registration: All-in-one node that can apply the following image registration techniques: Translation, Rigid (translation + rotation), Similarity (translation + rotation + isotropic scaling), Affine, Elastic (BUnwarpJ with cubic B-splines), Moving least squares. This node applies a pair-wise registration where the target image is registered to the reference image.
ij1-threshold-auto2d: Applies an auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This node requires 8-bit images and uses 256 bins (one per pixel value). Use 'Auto threshold 2D (16-bit)' or 'Auto threshold 2D (custom bins)' for images with a higher bit depth.
ij1-threshold-auto2d-16u: Applies an auto-thresholding algorithm to 16-bit images. The threshold is calculated from the full-range 65536-bin histogram (one bin per pixel value), so no precision is lost. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-auto2d-nbins: Applies an auto-thresholding algorithm to a histogram with a custom number of bins. 8-bit and 16-bit inputs are binned over their full native range. For 32-bit inputs, the bin range is determined by the multi-slice thresholding mode: 'Apply threshold per slice' uses each slice's minimum/maximum, 'Combine slice statistics' uses the whole image's minimum/maximum, and 'Combine thresholds per slice' computes per-slice thresholds that are combined via the expression. The threshold is mapped back to a pixel value via the bin range. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-expression2d-16u: Allows to implement a custom thresholding method via expressions. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-expression2d-16u-v2: Allows to implement a custom thresholding method via expressions. This node supports the calculation of both the minimum and maximum thresholds.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-expression2d-32f: Allows to implement a custom thresholding method via expressions. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-expression2d-32f-v2: Allows to implement a custom thresholding method via expressions. This node supports the calculation of both the minimum and maximum thresholds.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-expression2d-8u: Allows to implement a custom thresholding method via expressions. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-expression2d-8u-v2: Allows to implement a custom thresholding method via expressions. This node supports the calculation of both the minimum and maximum thresholds.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-expression2d-color: Applies a mathematical operation to each pixel to convert the color into a greyscale value.
ij1-threshold-local-auto2d: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm.  This node supports various methods:  Mean (threshold is mean local pixel value) Median (threshold is median local pixel value) MidGray (threshold is average of min and max pixel values) Otsu (threshold is the local otsu threshold)  If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.
ij1-threshold-local-auto2d-16u: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm.  This node supports various methods:  Mean (threshold is mean local pixel value) Median (threshold is median local pixel value) MidGray (threshold is average of min and max pixel values) Otsu (threshold is the local otsu threshold)  If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-local-auto2d-16u-bernsen: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.  Bernsen recommends a radius of 15 and a contrast threshold of 15.
ij1-threshold-local-auto2d-16u-niblack: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-local-auto2d-16u-phansalka: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. The threshold is calculated as t = mean * (1 + p * exp(-q * mean) + k * ((stdev / r) - 1)). If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-local-auto2d-16u-sauvola: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-local-auto2d-bernsen: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.  Bernsen recommends a radius of 15 and a contrast threshold of 15. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.
ij1-threshold-local-auto2d-niblack: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.
ij1-threshold-local-auto2d-phansalkar: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. The threshold is calculated as t = mean * (1 + p * exp(-q * mean) + k * ((stdev / r) - 1)). If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.
ij1-threshold-local-auto2d-sauvola: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.
ij1-threshold-manual2d-16u: Thresholds the image with a manual threshold. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-manual2d-32f: Thresholds the image with a manual threshold. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-manual2d-8u: Thresholds the image with a manual threshold. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-percentile2d-16u: Thresholds the image with a threshold calculated from the image pixel values (percentile of the 65536-bin histogram). If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-threshold-percentile2d-8u: Thresholds the image with a threshold calculated from the image pixel values. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-transform-add-border-2d: Adds a border around the image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-transform-crop-to-roi: Crops the incoming images to fit into the boundaries defined by the ROI. Alternative: Extract to ROI
ij1-transform-crop2d: Crops a 2D image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-transform-equalize-dimensions: Makes the input image have the same dimensions as the reference image. You can choose to make them equal in width/height, and hyperstack dimensions (Z, C, T)
ij1-transform-equalize-dimensions-max-io: Makes the input image have the same dimensions as the maximum of all images. You can choose to make them equal in width/height, and hyperstack dimensions (Z, C, T). Optionally annotates each output with information about its original size. This node allows multiple inputs and outputs (IO-configuration). The maximum is calculated over all inputs and then returned via the corresponding output.
ij1-transform-equalize-expand2d: Makes all images within a iteration step have the same size by padding with the predefined background color according to the largest image dimensions. If you want more control (source/target) and/or also want to do the same  for Z/C/T, use 'Equalize hyperstack dimensions'
ij1-transform-expand2d: Pads each image slice with a background color.
ij1-transform-flip2d: Flips the image vertical or horizontal. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-transform-line-mirror-by-expression: The two endpoints of a line a provided via expressions. The resulting line is used as axis to mirror the image pixels. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-transform-line-mirror-by-roi: The two endpoints of a line a provided via one or multiple line ROI. If multiple ROI are provided, the algorithm is executed per ROI. If a ROI is not a line ROI, a line outline/hull operation is applied to the ROI (see Outline 2D ROI).The resulting line is used as axis to mirror the image pixels. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-transform-rotate2d: Rotates the image in 90° steps to the left or to the right. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-transform-rotate2d-free: Rotates the image by any kind of angle. Expands the canvas if necessary. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-transform-scale2d: Scales a 2D image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij1-transform-set-dimensions: Sets the exact hyperstack dimensions of the incoming images. If you provide a lower size, planes will be removed. If you provide a larger dimension, planes are either set to black or copied from the slices with the highest index.
ij1-transform-tile-2d: Splits the image into tiles of a predefined size. If the image is not perfectly tileable, it is resized.
ij1-transform-tile-2d-v2: Splits the image into tiles of a predefined size. If the image is not perfectly tileable, it is resized.
ij1-transform-un-tile-2d: Merges/Assembles multiple image tiles back into one image. Utilizes annotations to determine the location of tiles.
ij1-transform-warp2d: Warps the image by applying a 2-channel vector field of relative coordinates where the pixels should be copied to. The vector field should either have the same dimensions as the input, or consist of only one plane, where it will be applied to all input planes.
ij1-turbo-reg-image-registration: Aligns the target image to the source image using methods implemented by TurboReg and MultiStackReg. Due to the variation in registration tasks, this node follows a 'rules' approach where each slice of the input image is matched to one rule that determines how the slice is aligned. There are three modes: (1) register to a reference slice, (2) use the same transformation calculated for another slice, and (3) apply no registration. Use the examples provided via the 'Tools' menu (top right of the parameter window) to get started with configuring the rules.  Handling of RGB images: as the underlying alignment methods were only designed for greyscale images, RGB slices are automatically converted to greyscale prior to registration (using ImageJ methods). The resulting transformation is then applied per RGB channel, which is then output.  Please note that if an RGB image is present, the output will be RGB. You may lose greyscale precision (16 bit/ 32 bit) in other slices. To prevent this, convert RGB to greyscale prior to registration (e.g. by splitting RGB channels into hyperstack channels).
ij1-turbo-reg-image-registration-io: Aligns slices in the input image to other slices using methods implemented by TurboReg and MultiStackReg. Due to the variation in registration tasks, this node follows a 'rules' approach where each slice of the input image is matched to one rule that determines how the slice is aligned. There are three modes: (1) register to a reference slice, (2) use the same transformation calculated for another slice, and (3) apply no registration. Use the examples provided via the 'Tools' menu (top right of the parameter window) to get started with configuring the rules.  Handling of RGB images: as the underlying alignment methods were only designed for greyscale images, RGB slices are automatically converted to greyscale prior to registration (using ImageJ methods). The resulting transformation is then applied per RGB channel, which is then output.  Please note that if an RGB image is present, the output will be RGB. You may lose greyscale precision (16 bit/ 32 bit) in other slices. To prevent this, convert RGB to greyscale prior to registration (e.g. by splitting RGB channels into hyperstack channels).
ij1-unsharp-mask-2d: Subtracts a blurred copy of the image and rescales the image to obtain the same contrast of large (low-frequency) structures as in the input image. This is equivalent to adding a high-pass filtered image and thus sharpens the image. "Radius (Sigma)" is the standard deviation (blur radius) of the Gaussian blur that is subtracted. "Mask Weight" determines the strength of filtering, where "Mask Weight"=1 would be an infinite weight of the high-pass filtered image that is added. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
ij2-create-out-of-bounds-factory: Defines an ImageJ2 Out Of Bounds factory
ij3d-analyze-find-particles: Finds 3D particles in a binary mask image and returns them as a list of 3D ROIs. It labels connected components, applies optional size, sphericity, edge, and background settings, and uses image calibration for physical measurements when available.
ij3d-binary-voronoi-3d: The Voronoi algorithm will draw lines between objects at equal distances from the boundaries of the different objects, then compute zones around objects based on these lines. This can also be seen as the splitting of the background.  Neighbouring objects can then be computed as objects having a line in common.
ij3d-binary-watershed-3d-splitting: The main application of watershed in ImageJ is the 2D splitting of merged objects.  This splitting is based on the computation of the Distance Map inside the mask of the merged objects. The seeds are then the local maxima of the distance map, the farthest points from the boundaries, hence corresponding to the centres of the objects. The bigger the object, the higher the values of the distance map at the centre, then the faster the growing of the seeds and the larger the resulting object.
ij3d-feature-canny-edge-3d: 3D Canny-Deriche edge detection filter. Will compute the gradients of the image based on the Canny edge detector.
ij3d-feature-maxima-local-3d: Detects local maxima with high contrast. Local maxima in a specified radius are computed and sorted by intensity. Starting from local maximum with highest intensity, a 3D flooding is performed, all connected pixels with values above the value of (LocalMaxima - NoiseValue) are marked as zone of the local maximum. All other local maxima from these zones are removed. The next local maximum is processed, this step is repeated until there are no more local maxima to process. The final image is created with local maxima, with their original intensity value.
ij3d-feature-symmetry-3d: Compute the gradients of the image based on the Canny edge detector. Then the symmetry filter will vote for the voxels inside the object based on the gradient vector direction.
ij3d-filter-adaptive-3d: Applies the 3D adaptive smoothing filter (similar to the Nagao filter) using an ellipsoidal neighbourhood.
ij3d-filter-close-3d: Calculates the morphological closing using an ellipsoidal neighbourhood.
ij3d-filter-local-max-3d: Calculates the 3D maximum in an ellipsoidal neighbourhood.
ij3d-filter-max-3d: Calculates the 3D maximum in an ellipsoidal neighbourhood.
ij3d-filter-mean-3d: Calculates the local 3D mean in an ellipsoidal neighbourhood.
ij3d-filter-median-3d: Calculates the local 3D median in an ellipsoidal neighbourhood.
ij3d-filter-min-3d: Calculates the local 3D minimum in an ellipsoidal neighbourhood.
ij3d-filter-open-3d: Calculates the morphological opening using an ellipsoidal neighbourhood.
ij3d-filter-roi3d-by-statistics: Keeps 3D ROIs that meet a condition based on their measured statistics. It takes a list of 3D ROIs and an optional reference image, calculates the selected measurements, and outputs the matching 3D ROIs as a new list.
ij3d-filter-roi3d-list: Only passes 3D ROI lists that match the filter criteria.
ij3d-filter-sobel-3d: Applies the 3D sobel filter using an ellipsoidal neighbourhood.
ij3d-filter-top-hat-3d: Calculates the morphological top-hat using an ellipsoidal neighbourhood.
ij3d-filter-variance-3d: Calculates the local 3D variance in an ellipsoidal neighbourhood.
ij3d-labels-to-roi: Turns a grayscale label image, where each object is marked, into a list of 3D ROIs. It detects separate marked objects, applies optional size, sphericity, and edge filters, and uses image calibration when available.
ij3d-math-distance-map-3d: Calculates the Euclidean distance map of a 3D image. The calculated distances will be in the calibrated unit.
ij3d-math-eroded-volume-fraction-3d: The EVF (Eroded Volume Fraction) can be regarded as a normalized EDT (Euclidean Distance Map). The calculated distances will be in the calibrated unit.
ij3d-measure-pairwise-roi3d: Extracts all pairwise statistics between the 3D ROI
ij3d-measure-roi3d: Generates a results table containing 3D ROI statistics. If a reference image is provided, the statistics are calculated for the reference image. Otherwise, NaN is returned.
ij3d-roi-calculator: Applies logical operations to the input ROI list. The logical operations are applied to the whole list, meaning that an AND operation will create the union of all ROI in the list. If you want to apply the operation only to a sub-set of ROI, preprocess using a ROI splitter algorithm.
ij3d-roi-change-properties: Updates every 3D ROI in a list of 3D ROIs by optionally setting its name, comment, center coordinates, channel, frame, and fill color, then outputs the updated list.
ij3d-roi-change-properties-from-expressi: Sets the properties of all 3D ROI via expressions
ij3d-roi-change-properties-from-table: Sets properties of all ROI to values extracted from a table. Table rows are matched to their ROI and the column values are put into expression variables, so the ROI can be modified.
ij3d-roi-color-by-name: Sets the 3D ROI item colors by their name.
ij3d-roi-color-by-statistics: Colors a list of 3D ROIs by a chosen measurement. It takes 3D ROIs and an optional reference image, measures the selected statistic for each ROI (in physical units when available), maps the values to a color map, and outputs the same 3D ROI list with updated fill colors.
ij3d-roi-convert-2d-to-3d: Converts a 2D ROI list into a 3D ROI list. Please note that you need to enable the fast mode to merge 2D ROI in the Z-axis.
ij3d-roi-convert-3d-to-2d: Converts a 3D ROI list into a 2D ROI list.
ij3d-roi-convert-to-3d-mesh: Takes a list of 3D ROIs and turns each into a 3D mesh, producing a 3D scene for visualization or downstream processing. It can respect physical voxel sizes, force a mesh length unit, smooth surfaces, add a name prefix, and override mesh color.
ij3d-roi-convert-to-labels: Converts 3D ROI lists to a label image. Depending on the number of objects, an 8-bit, 16-bit, or 32-bit label image is generated.
ij3d-roi-convert-to-mask: Takes a list of 3D ROIs and an optional reference image, then creates a greyscale mask image marking the 3D pixels covered by the ROIs. The mask matches the reference image size when one is supplied; otherwise it is sized to the ROIs.
ij3d-roi-convert-to-rgb: Converts 3D ROI lists to a label image. Depending on the number of objects, an 8-bit, 16-bit, or 32-bit label image is generated.
ij3d-roi-extract-metadata: Extracts the metadata (properties map) of each 3D ROI and writes them into a table
ij3d-roi-filter-by-overlap: Filters the 3D ROI lists by testing for mutual overlap. The ROI1 output contains all ROI1 input ROI that overlap with any of ROI2. The ROI2 output contains all ROI2 input ROI that overlap with a ROI1 ROI.
ij3d-roi-filter-by-overlap-v2: Filters the 3D ROI lists by testing for mutual overlap. The ROI1 output contains all ROI1 input ROI that overlap with any of ROI2. The ROI2 output contains all ROI2 input ROI that overlap with a ROI1 ROI.
ij3d-roi-outline: Converts the ROI into bounding boxes, convex hulls, etc.
ij3d-roi-remove-border: Removes 3D ROI at the image borders
ij3d-roi-remove-metadata: Allows to filter/remove specific ROI metadata entries
ij3d-roi-set-metadata-from-table: Sets the 3D ROI metadata (property map) from a table. The table either has a column that indicates the ROI index or contains one row per ROI (row index is the ROI index)
ij3d-roi-set-overlay: Set overlay ROIs. Please note that 3D overlays are not natively supported by ImageJ.
ij3d-roi-split-by-statistics: Splits the incoming 3D ROI lists by a classifier value that is calculated based on statistics.
ij3d-roi-split-explode: Splits the 3D ROI lists into individual 3D ROI lists.
ij3d-roi-split-into-connected-components: Splits the input 3D ROI list into multiple ROI lists, one per connected component
ij3d-segmentation-hysteresis: Will perform 3-levels thresholding based on two thresholds. The low threshold will determine background (for values below), the high threshold the objects cores (for values above) and an intermediate level for values between low and high threshold.
ij3d-segmentation-iterative-thresholding: Tests all thresholds and detect objects for all thresholds, it will then try to build a lineage of the objects detected, linking them from one threshold to the next threshold, taking possible splits into account.
ij3d-segmentation-nuclei-3d: This plugin is designed to segment nuclei from cell culture (not from tissues). The method is based on a maximum Z-projection followed by a 2D Segmentation. The segmentation for the 2D projection is based on a global thresholding. The nuclei are then segmented and separated using ImageJ watershed.
ij3d-segmentation-spot3d-constant: The node works with two images, one containing the seeds of the objects, that can be obtained from local maxima (see 3D Filters or 3D Maxima Finder), the other image containing signal data. The program computes a local threshold around each seeds and cluster voxels with values higher than the local threshold computed. The same threshold will be applied to all the objects. This threshold is defined by the user as Local Background
ij3d-segmentation-spot3d-difference: The node works with two images, one containing the seeds of the objects, that can be obtained from local maxima (see 3D Filters or 3D Maxima Finder), the other image containing signal data. The program computes a local threshold around each seeds and cluster voxels with values higher than the local threshold computed. A constant difference is used to compute local threshold. The local threshold value is then computed as ValueOfSeed – diff.
ij3d-segmentation-spot3d-gaussian-fit: The node works with two images, one containing the seeds of the objects, that can be obtained from local maxima (see 3D Filters or 3D Maxima Finder), the other image containing signal data. The program computes a local threshold around each seeds and cluster voxels with values higher than the local threshold computed. First the radial distribution of the object is computed (see plugin 3D Radial Distribution), as concentric circles centred on the seed define growing regions of interest in which mean intensity values are measured. A gaussian fit of the radial distribution is computed in a given radius around the seed (Radius Max, in pixels)
ij3d-segmentation-spot3d-local-mean: The node works with two images, one containing the seeds of the objects, that can be obtained from local maxima (see 3D Filters or 3D Maxima Finder), the other image containing signal data. The program computes a local threshold around each seeds and cluster voxels with values higher than the local threshold computed. Three circles are drawn. The user defines the radius (in pixels) of each circle, given that the first circle should be located within the object, while the two other circles should be located outside of the object. The mean intensities of the object (within the first circle), and of the background (in between the two other circles) are measured and the threshold calculated. By default, the threshold is the mean of the two mean intensity values (weight=0.5). The user can however shift this parameter: for a weight value of 0.75, the threshold will be closer to the background value.
ij3d-segmentation-watershed-3d: The 3D Watershed operation works with two images, one containing the seeds of the objects, that can be obtained from local maxima (see 3D filters), the other image containing signal data. A first threshold1 is used for seeds (only seeds with value > threshold1 will be used). A second threshold is used to cluster voxels with values > threshold2. In this implementation voxels are clustered to seeds in descending order of voxel values.

opencv-filter-bilateral: Applies the bilateral filter to an image.  The function applies bilateral filtering to the input image, as described in http://www.dai.ed.ac.uk/CVonline/LOCAL_COPIES/MANDUCHI1/Bilateral_Filtering.html bilateralFilter can reduce unwanted noise very well while keeping edges fairly sharp. However, it is very slow compared to most filters.  Sigma values: For simplicity, you can set the 2 sigma values to be the same. If they are small (< 10), the filter will not have much effect, whereas if they are large (> 150), they will have a very strong effect, making the image look "cartoonish".  Filter size: Large filters (d > 5) are very slow, so it is recommended to use d=5 for real-time applications, and perhaps d=9 for offline applications that need heavy noise filtering.

project-user-directory: Returns a project user path as data. You can configure paths within the project settings.
python-script: Runs a Python script that has direct access to all input data slots. This node uses Jython, a Java interpreter for Python that currently does not support native functions (e.g. Numpy), but can access all Java types.Access to the iteration step is done via a variable 'data_batch' that provides access to all input and output data, as well as annotations. Input slots can be accessed from variables 'input_slots' (array), 'input_slots_map' (map from name to slot). The first (and only) input slot is also accessible via the 'input_slot' variable. python-script-merging: Runs a Python script that iterates through each iteration step in the input slots. r-script-iterating:
Allows to execute a custom R script. The script is repeated for each iteration step. Please note the each iteration step only contains one item (row) per slot. The script comes with various API functions and variables that allow to communicate with JIPipe:
  • JIPipe.InputSlotRowCounts contains named row counts for each slot. Is always 1 for each slot.
  • JIPipe.TextAnnotations contains the list of annotations (named strings)
  • JIPipe.Variables contains the list of variables defined by parameters (named values). If a parameter's unique key is a valid variable name, it will also be available as variable.
  • JIPipe.GetInputFolder(slot, row=0) returns the data folder of the specified slot. The data folder contains the input row stored in standardized JIPipe format.
  • JIPipe.GetInputAsDataFrame(slot, row=0) reads the specified input data row as data frame.
  • JIPipe.AddOutputFolder(slot, annotations=list()) adds a new output folder into the specified output slot and returns the folder path. Optionally, you can assign annotations to add as list of named strings. Please note that the folder must contain data according to the slot's data type (an image file or a CSV file respectively)
  • JIPipe.AddOutputDataFrame(data, slot, annotations=list()) adds the specified data frame into the specified output slot. Optionally, you can add annotations to the data.
  • JIPipe.AddOutputPNGImagePath(data, slot, annotations=list()) generates an image file path to be added as output and return the path. Please note that you must use png() or other functions to actually write this file.Optionally, you can add annotations to the data.

remove-array-annotations: Removes annotations or annotation columns that contain array values. Array values are valid JSON arrays encased in [ and ].
remove-data-annotations: Removes data annotations by their column name. Data annotations are different to string annotations and contain data instead of strings.
remove-na-annotation-columns: Removes annotation columns that have missing values.
rename-annotation: Renames one or more text annotations on each data item by matching old annotation names and replacing them with new names. It takes data items with text annotations and outputs the same items with the renamed annotations, leaving their values unchanged.
rename-data-annotation: Renames one or multiple data annotations.
render-jipipe-project: Creates a single-image render of a whole JIPipe pipeline project. This node is equivalent to Publish > Whole-pipeline render. Please note that the pipelines should be arranged in a space-efficient way to reduce the file sizes.
run-expression: Passes data through from the input to the output and runs the expression for each incoming data row. The result of the expression may or may not be used as annotation.
scene-3d-create-line: Generates a 3D scene containing a line mesh.
scene-3d-create-sphere: Generates a 3D scene containing a sphere mesh at the specified location.
select-data-table-rows: Allows to select the only a specific set of input data table rows. All other rows are not stored in the output.
select-path-interactive: Asks for a path (file/folder) interactively when the node is run. Currently not recommended. Use project user paths instead.
set-imagej-bioformats-settings: Sets the settings of an OME image that will be used to write the image into an *.ome.tif file.
set-imp-image-alpha: Sets the alpha channel of an IMP image from a mask
simplify-annotations: Merges multiple annotations that are used for iteration step generation into a single annotation. Deletes or downgrades annotations that were involved in the merge.
sleep: Waits/sleeps the specified time and proceeds to pass the input to the output unchanged
sort-rows-by-annotation: Sorts the data rows by one or multiple annotations.
sort-rows-by-expression: Sorts the data rows by one or multiple values that are extracted via expressions.
split-imp-image-alpha: Splits the alpha channel of IMP images into a dedicated image
table-add-annotation-columns: Adds column annotations to the table as new columns.
table-add-columns-generate: Adds a new column. By default no changes are applied if the column already exists. Can be optionally configured to replace existing columns.
table-add-missing-rows-in-series: Adds missing rows in a table that contains a numeric series of rows (e.g., a time series)
table-annotate-by-merged-columns: Copies column values into an annotation. If the column has different values, the annotations are merged according to the selected merging strategy.
table-annotate-with-properties: Annotates tables with information about the table
table-apply-expression-per-row: Deprecated. Use the node with the same name. Applies an expression for each row. The column values are available as variables.
table-apply-expression-per-row-v2: Applies an expression for each row. The column values are available as variables.
table-apply-expression-to-table-by-colum: Applies an expression to the whole table. Each entry in the list of processors generates a column.
table-column-to-numeric: Converts one or multiple columns into a numeric column
table-column-to-string: Converts one or multiple columns into a string column
table-convert-columns: Applies a converting function to all column values. The result of the operation is stored in the same or a new column.
table-convert-to-count-column-value-occu: Counts the values in the provided column and outputs a table with the number of occurrences of each value. This node supports string columns and converts numeric columns into string columns. Null values are replaced with empty strings.
table-convert-to-histogram: Deprecated. Replace with a new node with the same name. Generates a histogram of table column values. Also supports weighting the values via an additional column.
table-convert-to-histogram-2: Generates a histogram of table column values. Also supports weighting the values via an additional column.
table-convert-to-histogram-key-value: Given a table with two numeric columns containing a key and a value, summarize all values assigned to a key into a single value. Allows the generation of normalized and cumulative histograms.
table-filter: Filters tables by iterating through each row and testing a filter expression.
table-filter-2: Keeps only tables that match a condition you write, such as having at least 10 rows or containing a named column. It checks each input table's row count, column count, column names, and annotations, and passes the table through unchanged when the condition is true; otherwise it produces no table.
table-integrate-columns: Summarize table columns by applying predefined operations like average, standard deviation, or median.
table-melt: Moves values from different columns (value columns) into their own rows, while the other columns are copied (category columns). Also known as unpivot operation.
table-merge-columns: Merges multiple tables into one table by merging the list of columns. The generated table is sized according to the table with the most rows. In missing columns, the values are filled in. The algorithm behind this is not 'smart' and is not capable of supplementing a table with data from another table.
table-merge-columns-supplement: Merges columns from the source table into the target table. You can choose one or multiple reference columns that determine which rows from each table should be merged together. Please note that this node can only merge two tables per iteration step. Use the 'Merge table columns (supplement)' node if you for example want to merge multiple sources into one/multiple target(s).
table-merge-columns-supplement-merge: Merges columns from the source table into the target table. You can choose one or multiple reference columns that determine which rows from each table should be merged together.
table-merge-from-columns: Merges multiple table columns into a table.
table-merge-tables: Merges multiple tables into one table by merging the list of rows. Columns are automatically created if they do not exist.
table-process-columns: Applies an expression function to all column values. The result of the operation is stored in the same or a new column. It is now recommended to use 'Apply expression to table (columns)' instead of this node.
table-remove-columns: Takes a results table and removes one or more columns whose names match the configured filter expression, producing a new results table without those columns.
table-rename-columns: Renames one or more columns in a results table by matching column names with the From entries and replacing them with the To entries. It takes a ResultsTableData table and outputs the same table with updated column headers.
table-rename-columns-2: Renames one or more columns in a ResultsTableData table and outputs the same table as ResultsTableData with updated column names. Each renaming entry matches an old column name and assigns a new name, optionally using the current name in an expression.
table-rename-columns-expression: Uses an expression to modify/rename table column names. If a renaming yields an existing column, it will be automatically renamed to be unique.
table-rename-columns-to-annotation: Sets the name of specified columns to the value of the specified annotations.
table-rows-dbscan-clustering: Applies DBSCAN (density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise) clustering on the table by extracting a feature vector per row and writes the cluster ID into a new column.
table-rows-fuzzy-kmeans-clustering: Applies Fuzzy K-Means clustering on the table by extracting a feature vector per row and writes the best-matching cluster ID and the memberships into a new column.
table-rows-kmeans-clustering: Applies K-Means clustering on the table by extracting a feature vector per row and writes the cluster ID into a new column. Also supports Multi-K-means clustering by applying multiple trials.
table-slice-rows: Allows to select/slice the only specific rows from the input table.
table-sort: Produces a sorted results table from an input results table, reordering rows by one or more selected columns. Columns can be matched by name filters, sorted ascending or descending, and strings can use natural order; an optional reverse switch flips the final order.
table-sort-columns: Sorts the table columns. Also allows to provide a manual sorting.
table-split-by-columns: Splits a table into multiple tables according to list of selected columns. Sub-tables that have the same values in the selected columns are put into the same output table.
table-split-into-columns: Splits a table into individual columns
table-split-into-rows: Splits a table into individual rows
table-to-csv-text: Converts a table to a text in CSV format
table-to-parameters: Converts a table into a parameter table. Please note that you have to define how each individual column is converted into a parameter. To do this, add an entry into the 'Table columns' list and provide the parameter key, parameter type, and from which table column the value is sourced.
table-unmelt: Moves values located in a value column into separate columns according to a set of categorization columns. Also known as dcast in R.
tables-from-expression: Generates a table from expressions that are applied for each table row, given by a parameter. Use 'Generate table columns from expression' if you want to do not know the number of rows.
tables-from-script: Executes a Python-script that generates a table. There must be an array 'tables' that contains all input rows as dictionary with following entries: 'data', 'nrow', and 'annotations'. 'data' is a dictionary with the column name as key and values being an array of strings or doubles. 'nrow' is an integer that contains the number of rows. 'annotations' is a dictionary from string to string containing all annotations
tesseract-ocr: Detects text in the image using Tesseract OCR. We highly recommend to preprocess the image by applying thresholding, otherwise Tesseract will apply its own Otsu-based method that may yield unsatisfactory results. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the OCR is applied per plane.
text-to-table-expression: Extracts a values from the input text data (via an expression) and writes the results into a table.
threshold-brightspots2d:
Applies thresholding by applying a background subtraction, auto thresholding, and various morphological operations. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
If you want to further customize all steps, create a group or set of nodes that apply the following operations:
  1. Subtract background (rolling ball): default radius = 20
  2. Auto threshold 2D
  3. Morphological dilation
  4. Morphological hole filling
  5. Morphological erosion
  6. Optional: Gaussian blur
threshold-by-annotation: Thresholds the image with a manual threshold provided by annotations. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
threshold-hessian2d:
Segments by applying a Hessian and morphological postprocessing. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
If you want to further customize all steps, create a group or set of nodes that apply the following operations:
  1. Calculate Hessian
  2. Morphological Internal Gradient
  3. Auto Threshold 2D
  4. Despeckle
threshold-hough2d: Finds circular 2D objects via a Hough transform. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
threshold-hough2d-fast: Finds circular 2D objects via a Hough transform. This implementation is based on code by Michael Closson and is generally faster than the other Hough-based segmentation. It outputs the segmented mask, the maximum Hough accumulator image, and a table of all detected circles (x, y, Diameter, and Score).If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
threshold-internalgradient2d:
Segments objects by finding the internal gradients. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
If you want to further customize all steps, create a group or set of nodes that apply the following operations:
  1. Optional: First CLAHE
  2. Optional: Gaussian filter
  3. Optional: Second CLAHE
  4. Auto Threshold 2D
  5. Morphological dilation
  6. Morphological hole filling
  7. Morphological erosion
threshold-iterative-by-roi-statistics-2d: Applies a ROI detection and measurement for each threshold value. Based on the user-provided ROI criteria the threshold is either accepted or rejected. Returns the mask with the first applicable threshold or an image with zero values. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
trackmate-detector: Detects spots in a 2D or 3D image using a configured TrackMate spot detector and returns them as a spots collection. It takes an image and the detector settings, runs TrackMate detection, and produces the detected spot positions and features for downstream tracking.
trackmate-filter-spots: Takes a TrackMate spot collection, keeps only detected spots that satisfy a per-spot expression, such as quality > 30, and outputs a filtered collection of the remaining spots.
trackmate-filter-tracks: Takes a TrackMate track collection (TrackCollectionData), keeps only the tracks that satisfy a per-track expression, and outputs a filtered TrackCollectionData with non-matching tracks hidden.
trackmate-measure-branches: Analyzes each branch of all tracks, and outputs in an ImageJ results table the number of its predecessors, of successors, and its duration.
trackmate-measure-edges: Measures the edges and outputs the results into a table
trackmate-measure-spots: Measures the spots and outputs the results into a table. If tracked spots are provided, the track ID will also be added.
trackmate-measure-tracks: Measures the tracks and outputs the results into a table
trackmate-merge-spots: Merges spot lists. Please ensure that the spots are sourced from the same image.
trackmate-merge-tracks: Merges track lists. Please ensure that the spots are sourced from the same image.
trackmate-split-spots: Creates a list for each individual spot
trackmate-split-tracks: Creates a list for each individual track
trackmate-spots-to-roi: Takes a collection of TrackMate spots and creates a list of 2D ROIs, one ellipse per spot, positioned at the spot's x, y, z, and time coordinates. The ROIs can be named and colored using spot features, and are output as a 2D ROI list for downstream analysis.
trackmate-tracking: Links detected spots into tracks using TrackMate. It takes a collection of detected spots and a configured spot tracker, then produces the resulting tracks.
trackmate-tracks-to-roi: Converts TrackMate tracks into ROI lists. Each lists contains the spot ROI of one track.
trackmate-visualize-follow-spots: For each track, generates an image that follows the spot over time
trackmate-visualize-spots: Renders detected spots and their tracks as a color image. It takes a spots collection and, optionally, a reference RGB image, draws the spots on each frame and Z slice, and produces a new RGB image with the same scale.
trackmate-visualize-track-scheme: Creates a visual track scheme image from a TrackMate track collection, showing each detected object and its connections over time as a diagram. The input is a TrackCollectionData and the output is an ImagePlusData containing the rendered scheme.
trackmate-visualize-tracks: Renders measured tracks as a color RGB image, optionally overlaid on a supplied RGB reference image. It takes a track collection and an optional RGB image, draws the tracks on every time and z slice using the track visualization settings and magnification, and produces a new RGB image with the same dimensions and scale.
tsoax-analyze-snakes: Parses existing results generated by TSOAX
weka-classification-2d: Classifies an image with a Weka model. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the classification is applied per slice. To obtain ROI from the generated labels, utilize the 'Labels to ROI' node.
weka-classification-3d: Classifies a 3D image with a Weka model. To obtain ROI from the generated labels, utilize the 'Labels to ROI' node.
weka-training-label-2d: Trains a Weka model on 2D image data that classified by a label image. Can only train on a single image. Use the multi-image node if you want to train from multiple images.
weka-training-label-2d-v2: Trains a Weka model on 2D image data that classified by a label image.
weka-training-mask-2d: Trains a Weka model on 2D image data that classified into two classes via a mask. Can only train on a single image. Use the multi-image node if you want to train from multiple images.
weka-training-mask-2d-v2: Trains a Weka model on 2D image data that classified into two classes via a mask.
weka-training-roi-2d: Trains a Weka model on 2D image data. The inputs are ROI that are assigned to the classes and trained on the input image. Can only train on a single image. Please convert ROI to labels/masks and use the appropriate nodes if you want to train on multiple images.
weka-training-roi-3d: Trains a Weka model on 3D image data. The inputs are ROI that are assigned to the classes and trained on the input image.Can only train on a single image. Please convert ROI to labels/masks and use the appropriate nodes if you want to train on multiple images.
xml-annotate-with-xml-data: Extracts a value from the input text data (via XPath) and annotates the data with the result. Please visit https://www.w3schools.com/xml/xpath_intro.asp to learn about XPath.
xml-extract-data-as-table-xpath: Extracts a value from the input text data (via XPath) and writes the results into a table. Please visit https://www.w3schools.com/xml/xpath_intro.asp to learn about XPath.
xml-extract-text-from-xpath: Extracts text data from from the input XML data (via XPath). Please visit https://www.w3schools.com/xml/xpath_intro.asp to learn about XPath.
xml-prettify: Takes in XML data and produces formatted XML data that is easier to read, using a configurable indentation level and optionally omitting the XML declaration.
